text: This story is the rwb-case app slice of RWB-E2-001: create or link the case from the hand-over and put the EFS history on the case; the ACE read, the hand-over adapter and the ingestion stay with rwb-integration and rwb-source-data.
why: The WP splits the legacy key and gives the APP work to P3 rwb-case with RWB-P2-E2001-CON as its only contract dependency, so the split boundary has to be stated.
read: WP B2-P3-020 story line; RWB E2 001 v1 s4 and s12; FSD P3 A2.27 and A2.30
confirm: Architecture owner, P2 and P3 leads
impact: If the boundary moves, the create-or-link and the ledger append move with it and the C dependency changes.

text: All ten acceptance criteria are new (D-RCV-60) and keep the legacy values, because the story line carries no legacy AC IDs to copy.
why: The story line lists no ACs while the legacy ACs of RWB-E2-001 are proved across services, so new criteria test only this deliverable.
read: WP B2-P3-020 acs: []; RWB E2 001 v1 s7
impact: The legacy ACs stay with the integration story; this story keeps the values so nothing is lost.

text: The interaction ledger is read and written through rwb-source-data's contract; rwb_case holds no interaction row and the P3 TSD interaction object is treated as owned by rwb-source-data.
why: DP-18 and the default ruling give the ledger to rwb-source-data, while the legacy story and the P3 data model still write it.
read: Template and Rules R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-18; TSD P3 v3 T3.1; context pack
confirm: Architecture owner and the ledger owner
impact: The ledger append becomes a contract call with its own failure path; the P3 ledger story needs re-scoping.

text: JOB-02 becomes the event-started workflow DailyCaseRun on task queue rwb-case, started by AceDataReady (EV-26) or AceDataLate (EV-27), with handover.hold_until 09:00 as a durable timer; a duplicate start returns the running execution and a rerun request answers 409 MSG-P2-006.
why: DP-10 replaces Quartz with the workflow kit, and the legacy hold and refusal behaviour has to be kept somewhere.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10; FSD P3 A1.5 trigger and A2.31; RWB E2 001 v1 s4 and s5 X6
impact: No Schedule row is created; the rerun operation still has to be fixed by a contract story.

text: The platform H dependencies that the DP table adds are held by the platform contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata Depends on (build) row, which is copied as None from the story line.
why: The WP copies H from the story line and lists no platform H dependencies, while the DP table adds six of them.
read: WP B2-P3-020 H: []; Template and Rules R5.5 and R5.7
confirm: Coordinator at step D1 and the lane planner
impact: The lane and the Day-1 allocation must carry the six platform CON stories, or the story is not buildable on Day 1.

text: The legacy test levels map System to Component, Access to Contract and Resilience to NFR, and the -ITG copies of the test cases belong to the wave 2 integration story.
why: The template fixes six levels and the legacy file uses System, Access and Resilience, so a mapping is needed and no level may be invented.
read: Template and Rules R7.2 s16; RWB E2 001 v1 s16
impact: The test pyramid stays as the legacy suite expects; the integration copies are planned with the ITG story.

text: RWB-P2-E2001-CON publishes the hand-over candidate page and the EFS history page that this story consumes, and the rwb-source-data contract stories publish the ledger append, the REC-05 break and the REC-01 result.
why: The story line gives RWB-P2-E2001-CON as the only contract dependency and DP-18 needs a P1 contract, so the resource split has to be assumed until the contracts are published.
read: WP B2-P3-020 C: [RWB-P2-E2001-CON]; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05, DP-11, DP-18
impact: If the split differs, the client and its fake change, but no business behaviour changes.

text: CaseCreated carries caseId, caseNo, productGroup, personKey, businessDate, accountKeys, entryDate and dpdAtEntry only, with the retry and dead-letter settings of the event platform, and a held run is resumed by the next AceDataReady while the screens show the last complete business date.
why: The sources name the event and the held-run messages but not the payload, the retry settings or the held state on the screens.
read: RWB E2 001 v1 s4 and s12; FSD P3 A2.31; Template and Rules R7.2 s17
confirm: Event platform owner and the data steward
impact: A wider payload would break the no-PII rule; the held state may need its own screen message.
